difficultyReason: Single causal inference with an obvious alternative explanation. The correct answer rules out that the increased fruit production was caused by seasonal rainfall rather than the new irrigation system.
stimulus: The introduction of a new irrigation system at Maple Farm resulted in a 40 percent increase in fruit production over the following season. Therefore, the new irrigation system is responsible for the increase in production.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Maple Farm had used irrigation systems at various points in its history.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Rainfall in the region was below average during the season in which production increased.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Other farms in the region also experienced increased production that season.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The new irrigation system was more expensive than the old one.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased fruit production is common when irrigation systems are first installed.

explanations.correct: By showing that rainfall was below average, this eliminates the alternative explanation that the increased production came from natural rainfall rather than the new irrigation system. This directly strengthens the causal claim.
explanations.A: Irrelevant to whether this particular new system caused the recent production increase.
explanations.C: Weakens the argument by suggesting a common regional cause rather than the unique new system at this farm.
explanations.D: Concerns cost, not whether the system caused the production increase.
explanations.E: While topical, this does not eliminate alternatives and actually suggests the increase might be a general phenomenon rather than caused specifically by this system.

difficultyReason: Straightforward causal argument where an obvious alternative explanation (existing technical ability) can be ruled out. Correct answer confirms the mechanism at work.
stimulus: After the hospital implemented a mandatory training program on patient safety procedures, the rate of medication errors dropped significantly. This suggests that the training program was the cause of the improvement.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to support the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Most hospital employees are willing to participate in training programs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Before the training program was implemented, staff members frequently made the same types of medication errors that the program addressed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Other hospitals have offered similar patient safety training to their staff.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The hospital's medication error rate had been stable for the five years before the training program.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some hospital staff members had prior experience with patient safety issues.

explanations.correct: By establishing that the error rate was stable before the training program, this rules out the alternative that some other gradual change (equipment upgrade, staffing change) caused the improvement. This directly strengthens the causal claim.
explanations.A: Irrelevant — willingness to participate doesn't establish the training caused the reduction.
explanations.B: While relevant to whether the training addressed the right problems, it doesn't eliminate alternative explanations for the improvement.
explanations.C: Other hospitals' practices are irrelevant to whether this hospital's training caused its improvement.
explanations.E: Doesn't address whether the training program caused the improvement.

difficultyReason: Simple causal argument about economic behavior. The correct answer rules out the alternative that price alone explains the sales increase, supporting the claim that advertising caused it.
stimulus: Last month, TechnoGear Company launched an aggressive advertising campaign for its new smartphone. Sales increased by 30 percent in the month following the campaign. Therefore, the advertising campaign was responsible for the sales increase.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The price of the smartphone remained unchanged during and after the advertising campaign.

choices.label: B
choices.text: TechnoGear Company had advertised previous products with moderate success.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The smartphone was more durable than competing products.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The advertising campaign reached millions of potential customers.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sales of other TechnoGear products also increased that month.

explanations.correct: By eliminating the alternative that a price reduction drove sales, this strengthens the claim that advertising was responsible. It shows the causal mechanism wasn't price-based.
explanations.B: Tells us about past campaigns but doesn't eliminate alternatives for this specific increase.
explanations.C: Product quality is a different alternative explanation that isn't ruled out by this choice.
explanations.D: Reach is consistent with advertising but doesn't rule out other causes of the sales increase.
explanations.E: Suggests a company-wide phenomenon rather than campaign-specific causation.

difficultyReason: Direct causal claim in environmental science with a clear alternative explanation. Correct answer rules out seasonal variation as the cause, strengthening the link to the new policy.
stimulus: Since the coastal city adopted a new waste-management policy that reduced plastic disposal in landfills, the amount of plastic debris in the nearby ocean has declined by 20 percent. Therefore, the policy directly reduced ocean plastic pollution.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ocean currents can transport plastic debris across thousands of miles.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Before the policy was adopted, the amount of plastic debris in the ocean had been increasing for consecutive years.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Other cities have implemented similar waste-management policies.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some of the plastic pollution in the ocean comes from sources outside the city.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Plastic debris in the ocean can harm marine wildlife.

explanations.correct: By showing a prior consistent upward trend, this rules out the alternative that ocean plastic naturally fluctuates seasonally or that the decline is unrelated to the policy. It strengthens the causal link.
explanations.A: Irrelevant to whether this city's policy caused the local decline.
explanations.C: Other cities' actions don't establish causation for this city.
explanations.D: While true, this doesn't rule out the policy being responsible for the decline.
explanations.E: Establishes the importance of the issue but not the causal claim.

difficultyReason: Causal argument in educational context with one clear alternative: student motivation rather than the new teaching method. Correct answer rules out this alternative.
stimulus: After introducing a new interactive teaching method, student performance on standardized tests improved by 15 percent. Consequently, the new teaching method is responsible for the performance improvement.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The new teaching method requires less preparation time than the traditional method.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Student motivation levels were comparable before and after the introduction of the new method.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Many schools have attempted to introduce new teaching methods.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The standardized test measures core academic skills.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Interactive teaching methods are popular in educational research.

explanations.correct: By establishing that student motivation remained constant, this rules out the alternative explanation that students simply became more motivated (rather than the method being more effective). This strengthens the causal claim.
explanations.A: Irrelevant to whether the method caused performance improvements.
explanations.C: Whether other schools use new methods doesn't establish causation here.
explanations.D: Confirms what the test measures but doesn't eliminate alternative explanations.
explanations.E: Popularity in research doesn't establish this method caused the improvement.

difficultyReason: Simple policy argument where the most obvious alternative is that external circumstances changed. Correct answer confirms the policy itself was the driver.
stimulus: The city enacted a new traffic law requiring mandatory traffic safety courses for repeat offenders. In the year following the law's implementation, traffic violations declined by 25 percent. The traffic law is therefore responsible for the reduction in violations.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Repeat offenders who completed the safety course reported that it increased their awareness of traffic hazards.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In the five years before the law was enacted, traffic violations had remained relatively stable.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Many cities have enacted similar mandatory safety course requirements.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The traffic safety course covers a wide range of driving scenarios.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some people who violate traffic laws do not repeat their offenses.

explanations.correct: By establishing that violations had been stable before the law, this rules out the alternative that some other external factor (better roads, improved vehicles, fewer drivers) caused the decline. This strengthens the causal claim.
explanations.A: Suggests a mechanism but doesn't rule out alternatives or establish the law specifically caused the decline.
explanations.C: Whether other cities have similar laws doesn't establish this law caused this city's decline.
explanations.D: Describes the course but doesn't connect it to causation of the decline.
explanations.E: About general patterns of re-offense, not about the specific law's effect.

difficultyReason: Straightforward technological causal claim where the alternative is that the result predates the intervention. Correct answer establishes timing to rule out pre-existing conditions.
stimulus: The software company implemented a new code-review process to reduce bugs in its applications. The number of reported bugs decreased by 35 percent in the three months after implementation. Therefore, the new code-review process caused the reduction.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The new code-review process requires developers to document their changes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In the twelve months before the new process was implemented, the number of reported bugs had been increasing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some applications are more prone to bugs than others.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Code-review processes are industry best practices.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The company's customers reported increased satisfaction with product reliability.

explanations.correct: By showing an upward trend in bugs before the process was implemented, this rules out the alternative that the bug reduction was part of a pre-existing trend. This strengthens the causal link to the new process.
explanations.A: Describes the process but doesn't establish it caused the reduction.
explanations.C: General variation in bug-proneness doesn't address whether this process caused this reduction.
explanations.D: Industry practice doesn't establish causation for this specific company's results.
explanations.E: Customer satisfaction follows from fewer bugs but doesn't establish the process caused the reduction.

difficultyReason: Simple causal claim in a linguistic/communication context. Correct answer rules out that the improvement was caused by something other than the grammar intervention.
stimulus: A writing instructor introduced daily grammar instruction in her composition class. After six weeks, students' written essays showed significantly fewer grammatical errors. Thus, the grammar instruction caused the improvement in essay quality.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Students in the class had completed fewer writing assignments before the grammar instruction began.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Writing proficiency is determined by many factors beyond grammatical accuracy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Before the grammar instruction began, students' essays showed no significant change in grammatical error rates across successive assignments.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The instructor provided feedback on grammar in addition to daily instruction.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some students in the class had prior instruction in grammar.

explanations.correct: By establishing that error rates were stable before instruction began, this rules out the alternative that students were improving on their own or that the improvement reflects natural maturation. This strengthens the causal claim.
explanations.A: Fewer assignments might weaken the argument by suggesting limited practice before instruction.
explanations.B: While true, this acknowledges multiple factors but doesn't establish the grammar instruction caused the improvement.
explanations.D: Feedback might be an alternative mechanism or confounding factor.
explanations.E: Prior experience doesn't address whether the current instruction caused the improvement.

difficultyReason: Causal argument about health intervention with one obvious alternative: the condition improving on its own. Correct answer rules this out.
stimulus: A clinic began administering a new treatment for a chronic skin condition. Patients receiving the treatment showed improvement in 80 percent of cases within four weeks. Therefore, the new treatment is responsible for the improvement.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The new treatment was developed after years of clinical research.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Patients with the chronic skin condition who did not receive the new treatment showed no improvement in the same four-week period.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The skin condition affects thousands of people worldwide.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some patients experienced minor side effects from the treatment.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Topical treatments are more commonly used than oral treatments for skin conditions.

explanations.correct: By establishing a control comparison where untreated patients showed no improvement, this rules out the alternative that the condition improves naturally over time. This directly strengthens the causal claim.
explanations.A: Research effort doesn't establish efficacy in practice.
explanations.C: Prevalence is irrelevant to whether the treatment caused the improvement.
explanations.D: Side effects might relate to safety but don't establish causation of improvement.
explanations.E: Treatment preferences don't address whether this particular treatment caused the improvement.

difficultyReason: Predictive/causal claim in historical context. Correct answer confirms the mechanism by which the policy is presumed to work, strengthening the argument.
stimulus: A museum installed improved climate-control systems in its rare manuscript collection room. Since the installation, the rate of deterioration of the manuscripts has slowed significantly. Therefore, the climate-control system is responsible for the slowdown.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The previous climate-control system was over fifty years old.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Temperature and humidity fluctuations are a primary cause of manuscript deterioration.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Many museums have upgraded their climate-control systems in recent years.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some of the manuscripts in the collection are from the eighteenth century.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The museum has also improved its security systems.

explanations.correct: By establishing that temperature and humidity fluctuations cause deterioration, this confirms the mechanism by which the new climate control would reduce deterioration. This strengthens the causal claim.
explanations.A: The age of the old system is irrelevant to whether the new system caused the improvement.
explanations.C: Whether other museums upgraded doesn't establish causation for this museum.
explanations.D: Age of manuscripts doesn't explain the slowdown in deterioration.
explanations.E: Security improvements address a different preservation concern.
